# ldfreq

**Reproducible lexical diversity, vocabulary profiles, and source-linked
corpus analysis in R.**

`ldfreq` measures lexical diversity and reference-vocabulary coverage
while keeping every score connected to the exact words counted,
preprocessing choices, coverage rates, and reasons for unavailable
values.

[2.0-dev site](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/) · [Stable
1.0.0 site](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/) · [Get
started](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/getting-started.html)
· [Function
reference](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/index.html)
· [Choosing
metrics](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/choosing-metrics.html)
· [Report an issue](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq/issues)

## Why ldfreq?

- **Auditable from raw text to model table**: Every result retains
  counted tokens (`$token_audit`), parameter settings, and explicit
  `status` / `missing_reason` fields—short or empty documents are never
  silently dropped or turned into zeros.
- **Unified single- and multi-document API**: Pass one document or a
  corpus table (`data.frame`, `tibble`, `data.table`, or named list) to
  the same entry points
  ([`lexdiv_metrics_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md),
  [`lexdiv_metrics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md),
  [`lexdiv_tokenize()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md),
  [`tubelex_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md),
  [`nj8_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md),
  [`lexdiv_norm_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_norm_profile.md)).
- **One cohesive workflow**: Compute 13 lexical-diversity measures and
  cross-definition variants, profile vocabulary against
  frequency/level/norm/word-family lists (`TUBELEX`, `New JACET 8000`,
  `BNC/COCA` 1k–25k bands, `MorphoLex`, or custom tables), extract 2- to
  12-word lexical bundles, and inspect source contexts with KWIC
  concordances, dispersion, collocations, and keyness.
- **Lightweight and R-native**: Requires only **2 runtime packages**
  (`digest` and `stringi`), runs offline out of the box, and produces
  publication-ready Base-R figures (`monochrome = TRUE` supported).

## Installation

The `main` branch hosts the **2.0.0 development series (`1.99.0.9000`)**
(R 4.1 or later), distributed directly via GitHub. It consolidates
single-document and batch functions into unified entry points and
standardizes argument names; review the migration notes in
[NEWS.md](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq/blob/main/NEWS.md)
before upgrading an existing 1.x analysis.

``` r

# 2.0.0 development series from GitHub main
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq@main")

# Or use remotes
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq@main")
```

To install the **stable 1.0.0 release** instead:

``` r

remotes::install_github("Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq@v1.0.0")
```

To install the 2.0.0 development build from a local source archive:

``` r

install.packages(c("digest", "stringi"))
install.packages("ldfreq_1.99.0.9000.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

### Migrating from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0-dev

- **Unified polymorphic entry points**:
  [`lexdiv_tokenize()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md),
  [`lexdiv_lemmatize()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md),
  [`lexdiv_flemmatize()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_flemmatize.md),
  [`lexdiv_metrics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md),
  [`lexdiv_metrics_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md),
  [`nj8_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md),
  [`tubelex_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md),
  and
  [`lexdiv_norm_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_norm_profile.md)
  accept both single-document inputs and multi-document tables or named
  lists directly. Former separate batch-suffixed exports are retired.
- **Standardized column and cache arguments**: Token/term column
  selectors across multi-document functions use `term_col` (paired with
  `id_col = "document_id"`), and resource-backed profilers accept
  `cache_dir = NULL`.
- **Recorded English defaults**: Raw-text tokenization defaults to
  `case = "lower", tokenizer = "english"`. Pass
  `case = "preserve", tokenizer = "unicode"` to reproduce 1.0.0 raw-text
  settings. See
  [NEWS.md](https://github.com/Ryuya-dot-com/ldfreq/blob/main/NEWS.md)
  for the complete migration table.

## Quick start

Pass one text or a document table (`data.frame` or `tibble`) to
[`lexdiv_metrics_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md).
English tokenization (`tokenizer = "english"`) and lowercasing
(`case = "lower"`) are used by default and recorded alongside the
results:

``` r

library(ldfreq)

essays <- data.frame(
  document_id = c("essay_01", "essay_02", "empty_doc"),
  text = c(
    paste(
      "Students compared two versions of a short story in their writing class.",
      "They marked repeated words and discussed how each writer introduced new ideas.",
      "One group revised the opening while another group examined the ending.",
      "After reading the stories again, the students explained their choices and",
      "saved both the original texts and their revised versions for later comparison."
    ),
    "A short draft with too few words for a 50-token moving window.",
    ""
  )
)

batch <- lexdiv_metrics_text(essays, metrics = c("ttr", "mattr", "hdd", "mtld"))
batch
#> <lexdiv_text_batch_results: 3 documents; 70 audited tokens>
#> <lexdiv_batch_results: 3 documents; 12 metric records; schema 0.1.0>
#>    document_id metric_id      value  status                    missing_reason  N  V
#> 1     essay_01       ttr  0.7931034      ok                              <NA> 58 46
#> 2     essay_01     mattr  0.8177778      ok                              <NA> 58 46
#> 3     essay_01       hdd  0.8312797      ok                              <NA> 58 46
#> 4     essay_01      mtld 78.4933333      ok                              <NA> 58 46
#> 5     essay_02       ttr  0.9166667      ok                              <NA> 12 11
#> 6     essay_02     mattr         NA missing too_short_for_requested_parameter 12 11
#> 7     essay_02       hdd         NA missing too_short_for_requested_parameter 12 11
#> 8     essay_02      mtld 40.3200000      ok                              <NA> 12 11
#> 9    empty_doc       ttr         NA missing                       empty_input  0  0
#> ...

# Reshape directly to a wide reporting table and plot available scores:
wide <- lexdiv_widen(batch, values_from = c("value", "status", "missing_reason", "N"))
plot(batch, metric_id = "mtld")
```

Note that `essay_02` (12 tokens) is computable algebraically under
partial-factor MTLD (`mtld_tail_only = TRUE`), whereas empirical
stability floors (typically `N >= 100` for MTLD) are evaluated
explicitly without altering scores via
[`lexdiv_screen_lengths()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_screen_lengths.md).

Inspect `batch$token_audit` to verify every counted word, or bridge raw
texts straight into corpus search and keyness with
[`lexdiv_as_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_import_annotations.md)
(preserving original casing and character offsets alongside normalized
`term` and `is_word`):

``` r

ann <- lexdiv_as_annotations(essays)
kwic <- lexdiv_concordance(ann, queries = list(story = "stor*"), valuetype = "glob")
plot(kwic, "story")
```

## Choose your workflow

Start with
[`lexdiv_metrics_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md)
for raw texts or
[`lexdiv_metrics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
for pre-tokenized words. Add the workflow tools below when your research
design or reporting task needs them.

| Research question | Main functions | Worked guide |
|----|----|----|
| How do lexical-diversity scores vary across texts or counting rules? | [`lexdiv_metrics_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md) → [`lexdiv_widen()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_widen.md) / [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) | [From text to report](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/from-text-to-report.html) |
| How do writers, tasks, or occasions compare in longitudinal designs? | [`lexdiv_plan()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_plan.md) → `lexdiv_metrics_text(..., plan = plan)` → [`lexdiv_screen_lengths()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_screen_lengths.md) → [`lexdiv_study_table()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_study_table.md) → [`lexdiv_study_model_data()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_study_table.md) | [Repeated observations](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/repeated-observations.html) |
| How frequent, familiar, or morphologically varied is the vocabulary? | [`tubelex_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md), [`nj8_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md), [`lexdiv_norm_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_norm_profile.md), [`lexdiv_family_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_family_profile.md) | [Corpus reference profiles](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/corpus-reference-profiles.html) |
| Which words, bundles, and contexts explain a corpus pattern? | [`lexdiv_as_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_import_annotations.md) → [`lexdiv_concordance()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md) / [`lexdiv_ngrams()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_ngrams.md) / [`lexdiv_collocations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_collocations.md) / [`lexdiv_keyness()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_keyness.md) | [Concordance & dispersion](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/concordance-and-dispersion.html) · [Keyness](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/keyness-comparison.html) |
| How do I analyze Japanese texts with morphological annotations? | [`lexdiv_import_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_import_annotations.md) → explicit unit/POS selection → diversity or norm profiles | [Japanese annotations](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/articles/japanese-annotations.html) |

For repeated runs and portable reporting, `ldfreq` also provides
reusable recipes and exports
([`lexdiv_recipe()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_recipe.md)
→
[`lexdiv_run_recipe()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_run_recipe.md)
→
[`lexdiv_write()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_write.md)),
saved-analysis comparison
([`lexdiv_compare_analyses()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_analyses.md)),
English/Japanese calculation descriptions
([`lexdiv_methods_text()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_methods_text.md)),
an installed CLI (`exec/ldfreq.R`), and a standard-library Python bridge
(`inst/python/ldfreq_r.py`).

## Optional reference data

`ldfreq` code is MIT licensed and installs **without** third-party
datasets. Core diversity metrics, custom norm/reference tables, and
corpus tools work completely offline. To use optional external resources
(`tubelex`, `nj8`, `morpholex`, `bnccoca`, `morphynet`), inspect their
license terms first and download only what you need:

``` r

info <- lexdiv_resource_info("tubelex")
file.show(info$notice_path)  # installed terms; no data download or internet needed
lexdiv_download_resources("tubelex", accept_license = TRUE)
```

## Citation

Cite the exact `ldfreq` version used in your analysis alongside the
relevant measurement methods and reference datasets:

``` r

citation("ldfreq")
```

The citation reports the installed version. Cite the stable 1.0.0
release and 2.0.0 development snapshots separately when both were used.

# Package index

## Package overview

High-level map of unified inputs, workflows, measurement boundaries, and
citations.

- [`ldfreq`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/ldfreq-package.md)
  [`ldfreq-package`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/ldfreq-package.md)
  : Reproducible Lexical Diversity and Frequency Profiles

## Lexical-diversity metrics and cross-definition variants

Compute eleven default lexical-diversity measures, moving-average MTLD,
experimental expected-TTR D, and cross-definition Maas/MTLD variants
from single documents or multi-document containers.

- [`lexdiv_metric_ids()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
  [`lexdiv_metrics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
  [`` `[`( ``*`<lexdiv_results>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_batch_results>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_results>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_metrics.md)
  : Compute Versioned Lexical-Diversity Metric Variants
- [`lexdiv_variant_metrics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_variant_metrics.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_variant_results>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_variant_metrics.md)
  : Explicit Maas and Sequential-MTLD Comparison Variants

Tokenize single texts or document tables, attach lemma or AntBNC flemma
layers, bridge raw texts into source-aligned corpus annotations, or
import Japanese and Penn MASC annotations.

- [`lexdiv_tokenize()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_preprocessing.md)

## Reference-vocabulary, level, and word-family profiles

Inspect license terms, download SHA-256-verified optional datasets, and
profile single documents or corpora with TUBELEX, New JACET 8000,
BNC/COCA 1k–25k word-family bands, MorphoLex, or MorphyNet.

- [`lexdiv_resource_info()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_resources.md)
  [`lexdiv_download_resources()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_resources.md)
  : Inspect and explicitly download optional reference data
- [`tubelex_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md)
  [`print(`*`<tubelex_profile>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md)
  [`print(`*`<tubelex_profile_batch>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md)
  [`plot(`*`<tubelex_profile_batch>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_profile.md)
  : Coverage-Aware TUBELEX Frequency and Prevalence Profile
- [`tubelex_diagnostics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/tubelex_diagnostics.md)
  : Tabulate TUBELEX profiles while retaining coverage and input
  conditions
- [`nj8_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexical_level_profile>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md)
  [`print(`*`<nj8_profile_batch>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md)
  [`plot(`*`<lexical_level_profile>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_profile.md)
  : Profile lexical coverage by New JACET 8000 frequency level
- [`nj8_diagnostics()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/nj8_diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnose NJ8 non-matches and lexical-unit transformations
- [`bnccoca_data()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/bnccoca_data.md)
  : Read Nation's BNC/COCA Level 6 Word-Family Lists
- [`lexdiv_family_profile()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_family_profile.md)
  : Count resource-defined word families while retaining source
  occurrences

  : Read the Cached MorphoLex English Database
- [`morphynet_read_derivations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/morphynet_read_derivations.md)
  : Read MorphyNet Derivational Relations from a Local File

## Custom lexical norms, overlap, and n-gram bundles

Apply custom familiarity/AoA/frequency tables, measure exact lexical
overlap or set coverage, and extract or compare 2- to 12-word n-grams.

  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_ngrams>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_ngrams.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_ngram_reference>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_ngrams.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_ngram_profile>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_ngrams.md)
  : Adjacent Bigrams and Trigrams with Local Reference Frequencies
- [`lexdiv_build_ngram_reference()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_build_ngram_reference.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_ngram_build>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_build_ngram_reference.md)
  : Build an N-gram Reference from Whole-Document Chunks
- [`lexdiv_compare_ngrams()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_ngrams.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_ngram_comparison>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_ngrams.md)
  : Compare N-gram References on the Same Target Items

## Study tables and source-linked corpus exploration

Prepare longitudinal mixed-model tables, search KWIC concordances, and
compute within-document dispersion, collocations, keyness, or response
pairs.

- [`lexdiv_study_table()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_study_table.md)

  : Join Planned Observations to Saved Measurements and Select Model
  Rows

  [`lexdiv_sort_concordance()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md)
  [`lexdiv_concordance_dispersion()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_concordance>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md)
  [`print(`*`<lexdiv_dispersion>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md)
  [`plot(`*`<lexdiv_concordance>`*`)`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_concordance.md)
  : Search Source-Aligned Words and Phrases and Inspect Their
  Distribution
- [`lexdiv_collocations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_collocations.md)
  : Count collocation opportunities and descriptive association scores
- [`lexdiv_keyness()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_keyness.md)
  [`lexdiv_keyness_concordance()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_keyness.md)
  : Compare word frequencies in explicit target and reference corpora
- [`lexdiv_compare_responses()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_responses.md)
  : Compare paired binary vocabulary responses with an explicit
  criterion

## Annotation review, alignment, and contextual models

Audit changed tags, align different segmentations, record human KWIC
disambiguation decisions, and evaluate external contextual model
proposals.

- [`lexdiv_compare_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_annotations.md)
  : Compare annotation versions on identical tokenized documents
- [`lexdiv_evaluate_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_evaluate_annotations.md)
  : Evaluate external annotation labels against an explicit reference
- [`lexdiv_align_annotations()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_align_annotations.md)
  : Align different token segmentations using original source positions
- [`lexdiv_ambiguity_review()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_ambiguity_review.md)
  : Review lexical candidates in their original contexts
- [`lexdiv_compare_ambiguity()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_compare_ambiguity.md)
  : Compare two contextual lexical-candidate reviews
- [`lexdiv_import_contextual()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_import_contextual.md)
  : Attach external model outputs to verified contextual occurrences
- [`lexdiv_evaluate_contextual()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_evaluate_contextual.md)
  : Compare contextual candidate scores with an explicit reference
  review
- [`lexdiv_score_contextual()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_score_contextual.md)
  : Score contextual candidates using separate labeled training examples
- [`lexdiv_amod_pairs()`](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/dev/reference/lexdiv_amod_pairs.md)
  : Extract source-linked adjective and common-noun dependency pairs

Connect corpus statistics back to exact source occurrences via KWIC
concordances, dispersion, collocations, keyness, ordination, and
dependencies.

learning (DDL) handouts from reviewed corpus examples.
